Select a row for scatter plots, both sessions and every hardware bag. Select a column heading to sort. Counts show what each value is computed from; trials or bags that returned nothing are excluded from the error. Simulators score trials against entity truth. Hardware takes one all-candidate median per bag against a human measurement, and 30 bags share one placement. Polar rows show the simulator run captured alongside sensor depth; the monocular capture is in the row details.

What stands out

  • Sensor depth with a silhouette is the strongest camera path. MAE 0.067–0.090 m in simulation, 0.127–0.129 m on hardware, for both projective and Euclidean.
  • Polar with a silhouette has the lowest hardware error, with caveats. 0.046 m on 41 of 48 bags. In simulation it trails sensor depth (0.127–0.198 m) and scores only 89–101 of 135 trials.
  • Monocular is worst in every environment, and reads too far. MAE 0.77–0.90 m on hardware, 0.99–1.96 m in simulation. Bias is positive in every run.
  • Silhouettes help sensor depth and polar, and hurt monocular. Every box-to-silhouette swap lowers MAE for sensor depth and polar, and raises it for monocular, in all three environments.

Estimator

Projective
Reduces masked depth pixels to one distance, then deprojects one representative pixel.
Euclidean
Deprojects masked depth into 3D points, isolates the foreground, then reduces to one coordinate.
Polar
Projects the 2D LiDAR scan into the image, keeps returns inside the mask, then reduces the near runs.

Mask

Box
The OWL detection box, which also contains non-target surfaces.
Silhouette
SlimSAM segmentation inside the box. An empty silhouette never falls back to the box.

Detection

Did OWL box what was there? Each frame is scored against the targets placed in that scene, because a simulated scene can hold several G1s while hardware holds one. Several boxes are only a problem when they exceed the targets present. The frames behind the misses are below.

Missed detections

Each cell counts one target in one session and condition, compared across the two simulators. Isaac misses less often, and nearly everything Gazebo detects, Isaac also detects. Why is not measured here.

Show
OWL box Expected position, missed here Same target, detected here

Simulators: a miss means no estimate was matched to that target in any frame of the trial, across 8 runs per simulator (2 sessions × 4 conditions). Each picture comes from a run where the miss happened, using a frame saved at the start of the trial; a “detected” picture is session 1, box, sensor depth. Hardware has no target labels yet, so only frames with no box at all count here, and a bag with boxes is not a confirmed hit. As a geometric check rather than a label, every hardware frame with a box has one overlapping the expected position by at least half of the smaller area. Expected positions combine the recorded reference with a standing G1 size, for orientation only. Frames are full 640 × 480, compressed as WebP.

One frame, as the estimators read it

These maps are the arrays the estimators received: full 640 × 480, no smoothing, one colour per stored value. Hover for the exact depth. Select a frame to see every pixel. Illustrative clear views, independent placements: simulated reference 2.650 m; hardware nominal 2.866 m.

0 m6 m12 m and above
No depth value, dropped before estimating

Depth is optical Z, not pelvis radial distance, stored here to the nearest millimetre. In the simulators, no-depth pixels are rays that hit no surface, above the simulated walls. On hardware they are stereo holes. At this size the page shows a sample of the pixels without blending them. Yellow: accepted OWL box and confidence. Simulator sensor and monocular maps come from separate condition runs of single_facing_03, session 1. Hardware maps share one RGB, bag 02 frame 100.

From pixels to a distance

Projective ranging on these frames, using the masks and code from each run. Depth pixels under the mask are all the estimator sees.

Range input
Mask
Used Rejected by isolation No depth

Each frame was recomputed with production code from the stored capture and mask; all 12 match the distance recorded by the run to better than 0.001 mm. One frame is not the result: the trial or bag value is reduced over many frames, so it can differ, most of all with monocular depth. Euclidean reconstruction starts from the same masked pixels, then isolates in 3D. Polar uses no depth map.

What differs between environments

Each row can move a result without any change in estimator quality.

InfluenceObserved difference / open conditionPotential consequence
Appearance and scene distributionRendered materials / lighting / lab props vs physical lighting, supports, screens and clipping; placements differDifferent detector confidence, masks and learned monocular scale; overall rates do not isolate a domain effect
Mask and foreground selectionBox includes non-target surfaces; silhouette changes both pixels and scan raysHardware bag 28 stereo: box ≈1.82 m / silhouette ≈2.98 m. Polar silhouette can help or remove useful returns
Reference point and uncertaintySimulator entity truth vs recorded human-measured marked-pelvis position; 30 hardware bags share one placement; 8 assume unchanged position after turnErrors against the supplied measurements are shown. Surface depth is not pelvis depth; total reference uncertainty is unquantified; shared placements are not independent physical trials
Reporting datumFrozen simulator front offset 0.250 m; hardware measured nominal 0.465 mUse each result’s own truth frame. A common datum requires translating forward coordinates before recomputing radius
Calibration and distortionNominal pinhole / internal TF vs recorded factory intrinsics and camera extrinsics; hardware distortion ignored by projectionBearing and pixel-to-ray differences, especially near image edges; extrinsic accuracy still matters
LiDAR formation and visibilitySimulated intersections / noise vs physical returns; low scan plane may hit supports, legs, cabinet or backgroundPolar can miss G1 or return another surface; successful estimate alone does not verify beam attribution
Time and selectionLive simulator 10 s windows vs deterministic hardware nominal-10-Hz sampling; nearest scan ≤50 ms; hardware exact stereo pairing missing twiceDifferent sampled frames and temporal correlations; movement would increase misalignment sensitivity
Association and denominatorsSimulator truth-based scoring assignment vs unannotated hardware candidates; multi-target scenes vs one physical G1Simulator gate / detector misses cannot be equated to hardware any-box or any-number counts
Execution, versions and repeatabilityImported simulator revisions / GPU sessions vs frozen CPU float32 hardware pass; Isaac session outputs vary; full scientific qualification pendingCheck model snapshots, dtype and code identity before attributing small differences; offline wall time is not live latency
